newsitem.title: KENYA: Q1 inflation surges in Kenya after drought.
newsitem.headline: Q1 inflation surges in Kenya after drought.

text.p: A severe decline in agricultural output in the first quarter of this year because of drought has forced a steep rise in inflation in Kenya, the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) said in a report on Wednesday.

"The overall three-months annualised inflation surged to 35.6 percent in March from 14.7 percent in February. The overall month-on-month inflation rose to 15.6 percent in March from 11.9 percent in February," the bank said in a report for April.

"Average inflation increased to 10.7 percent from 9.9 percent," the bank said, adding that the unweighted food price index for Kenya's main three income groups increased by 43 percent in the year to March 1997 compared to an earlier increase of 17 percent in the same period last year.

The bank said overall inflation was expected to fall by June as the food supply situation improved following the start of the seasonal long rains in April. Financial experts have cast doubt on such plans in view of general elections later in the year.

The bank said the other significant reason for the upsurge in inflation included delayed effects of frequent adjustments in the prices of petroleum and petroleum-related products, especially since the last quarter of 1996.
"This has adversely affected transport and transport-related charges and indirectly influenced the pricing of a wide range of manufactured goods and other inter-related services," it said.

The bank said the price of kales had risen by 152 percent per kg in March from January, while those of cabbages rose 65 percent, maize floor 10 percent, maize 18 percent, and beans 44 percent in the same period. These are Kenya's staple foods.
